summary: Windows and browser selection toolbars archive selected roots through current Owner authorization and store::archive_selected_roots. Single and batch lifecycle actions share locked eligibility, state and revision rules. Each batch commits all selected states, one board revision and one command-bound receipt atomically. Existing single-item contracts and legacy receipts remain intact; recovery reads never resubmit an uncertain write.
evidence: Runner verified 51: 49 browser journeys, 28 Windows journeys, 41 host checks, locked workspace tests, runner regressions and formatting passed.

Source-derived expectations, not a new executed comparison: packets/51-selected-root-archive.md, 36-browser-selection-group-move.md and 37-browser-root-archive-restore.md supply the approved ordered selection, confirmation/recovery destination, root eligibility and restore-in-place behavior. No fresh reference application comparison was executed in this packet; the runtime results below are boardcraft checks.

cargo test --locked -p boardcraft-desktop --features native-smoke --test windows_smoke windows_archives_selected_roots -- --exact --test-threads=1 --nocapture passed. Twelve isolated live Windows scenarios exercised actual Kit checkboxes, folding, toolbar, dialog, Escape/focus restoration, Tab/Enter confirmation, pending suppression, Archive inventory and restore-one. Conflict, deferred commit refusal, missing original root, failed review/retry, demotion, lost membership/session, lost acknowledgment, failed refresh and Member/Viewer selection were checked against fresh whole-store reads. Review/adoption did not write; uncertain recovery did not send a second command.

cargo test --locked -p boardcraft-mobile-edit-host --features browser-smoke --test browser_preview browser_archives_ -- --test-threads=1 --nocapture passed all three focused journeys: selected-root archive plus the inherited single-root and group archive/restore journeys. The selected-root journey covered eleven isolated scenarios in owned headless Chromium profiles, including failed save/review, unavailable original target, current-access loss and uncertain-result read barriers. Captured methods, selected-board paths, statuses, ordered targets, revisions and operation identity agreed with independent database snapshots.

Both clients selected [67,59,61], retained the hidden 59 selection in folded g-20 through cancellation, then archived exactly those roots. After the presentation save, board revision advanced 2 to 3 once; selected item revisions advanced 1 to 2 without changing groups, positions, field stamps or creation provenance. Archive contained [57,59,61,67], with 57 still group-blocked. Restoring 67 alone advanced it to Active/3 and board/4, returned it between 73 and 77, and left 59 and 61 archived. Other records, groups, boards and saved folds stayed unchanged.

cargo test --locked -p boardcraft-mobile-edit-host --test loopback_board_access selected_root_archive_is_atomic_and_authorized -- --exact --nocapture passed. Real matched preview and native bearer requests used different sessions, rejected empty/duplicate/nil/oversized targets, stale board or one-item revisions, missing/foreign/hidden/Deleted/Staging roots and unauthorized roles/scopes. A 10,000-target missing list reached target validation; 10,001 targets were rejected. Deferred receipt failure rolled back the entire batch. Competing native/preview commands at one baseline produced one winner and one conflict. Exact replay returned the original acknowledgment without writing; changed content/order/revisions, another Owner and operation-kind collisions were refused. Replay still required current Owner, membership and live session access.

The same host case upgraded a populated v11 schema twice, preserving item records and successfully replaying pre-upgrade single-root and selection-move receipts while refusing reuse for batch archive. cargo test --locked -p boardcraft-mobile-edit-host --test loopback_board_access preview_root_lifecycle -- --test-threads=1 --nocapture also passed both inherited lifecycle access/visibility/replay cases, including their older migration fixtures.

Focused reused-selection regressions passed: windows_moves_selected_roots_to_group in the native-smoke windows_smoke target and browser_moves_toolbar_selection_in_request_order in the browser-smoke browser_preview target. The original move dialog, toolbar ordering, append behavior, selection, drafts and fold journey remained working.
